note: The official NeurIPS proceedings confirm the 2017 Transformer paper. Used as the attention foundation; its translation data are not local project datasets.
NAACL-HLT 2019 record confirms authors and title. This is the actual encoder lineage used through the pinned base uncased artifact.
The 2019 arXiv record is correct. RoBERTa is discussed as pretraining-control context; no RoBERTa checkpoint or corpus is used here.
Findings of EMNLP 2020 confirms the citation. The project extension is exBERT-inspired and is not an exact architecture or biomedical-training reproduction.
The full title ends with 'for biomedical text mining'. The issue year is 2020 although advance online publication was September 2019. No BioBERT weights or biomedical corpora are used.
The arXiv version lists Minho Ryu and Kichun Lee. A later 2022 journal version also lists Geonseok Lee; these are different bibliographic versions. Distillation is not implemented in this project.

The publisher index identifies IEEE CSDE 2023, not APSCDE. Title and five authors match. DOI is 10.1109/CSDE59766.2023.10487678. Full paper access was unavailable, so detailed experimental claims are not used.

The PDF cover identifies KTH, the exact supplied thesis title and 14 January 2026. The arXiv landing title adds Kullback-Leibler-Based; v1 is August 2025 and v2 is January 2026. No self-distillation run is claimed here.

The CVPR author paper confirms the title and authors. It studies visual-language knowledge, not the correctness of generated DFA diagrams. It is contextual only; this project has no vision-language pretraining.

The publisher gives 'a named entity recognition model', Cybersecurity volume 9, article 146, published 2 April 2026. It concerns cyberspace NER, not automata inference. Its datasets are not project inputs.

arXiv:2606.28538 confirms Stammbach and Henderson. It adapts ModernBERT in law, whereas this project uses original base uncased BERT and supervised formal outputs. Legal corpora and checkpoints are not used.
EMNLP 2016, pages 1918-1923, DOI 10.18653/v1/D16-1197. This is the directly relevant natural-language regex paper and repository lineage for the filtered KB13 mirror.
The author arXiv PDF states ICLR 2023; its initial preprint is 2022. Its generalization study motivates careful formal-task boundaries, not a claim that this prototype reproduces the study.
TACL volume 12, pages 543-561, 2024, DOI 10.1162/tacl_a_00663. The survey highlights architecture-dependent assumptions; it does not prove that this BERT system solves all formal languages.
ACL confirms EMNLP 2023, pages 5778-5791, DOI 10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.353. Its Wikidata semantic parser is relevant background; no WikiWebQuestions/Wikidata data or LLaMA/GPT route is used here.
